segments: Eighteenth Dynasty.
The Arab Kings.
and the Hospitallers,
and they demanded from the lord of Hamah thousands of dinars, the tribute that was owed by him.
And when he treated them with contempt and did not give [it],
five hundred knight brothers assembled,
and two thousand and seven hundred foot-soldiers,
and they came to conquer the territory of Hamah.
And Taqī al-Dīn went out and encountered them,
and he defeated them.
And in the year
one thousand five hundred and forty-two
[1542] of the Greeks, the Tatars pursued after the Khwarazmians,
and the Khwarizmshah fled towards Syria.
And they overtook him in the territory of Amid,
and they destroyed the army that was with him.
And he alone escaped from the Tatars,
and he went up into one of the mountains of Sophanene.
And there, the Kurds, not knowing who he was, killed him.
And some say
that it was the keeper of his clothes who was killed,
while he escaped and put on the clothes of the one who was killed,
which were of wool,
and he wandered through the lands secretly.
Now a legion of the Tatars entered the territory of Hisn Ziyad,
and reached as far as the Euphrates in the border of Melitene,
and crossed into the plain of Hanazit.
And because all the people had fled in terror from them to fortified places {OCR?: steep/lofty places} and to fortresses,
there was no great slaughter.
And those Tatars turned back and ruled over Adurbaygan and Shahrazur,
and they also subjugated the Iberians (Georgians).
And Muzaffar al-Din heard [of this] and was afraid,
and he sent asking for help from the Caliph.
And there was sent to him Jamal al-Din Qashtamur with a large army.
Now the remnant of the Khwarazmians who remained, about ten thousand, took refuge with Sultan Ala al-Din, the lord of the Romans (Rûm),
and they gave them lands for their sustenance.
And they remained in his servitude until he died.
At this time, Ögedei Khan, the son of Genghis
Khan, when he took over the kingdom of the Mongols,
led a large army and went to the lands of the outer Chinese, that is, the Cathayans who are called Khata.
And at first, they attacked a city named Kūgbānūtaqsīn, which was on the great river called Qara Muren,
and in it were twenty (ten) thousand warriors.
